_note: Test fixture: the date policy of briefs/brief-a.md, written by hand. At build time the builder extracts this from the brief.

source: The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock.
Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
| 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |
A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

on_non_business_day.say: <NAMED> is not a business day. The next business day is <DATE>. Could you pay on <DATE>?
source: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day.

on_after_deadline.say: The latest date I can record is <DEADLINE>. Could you pay on <DEADLINE>?
source: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it.

on_vague.say_ask: Which exact day would that be?
on_vague.say_final: Then I can offer <DEADLINE>, the latest date I can record. Could you pay on <DEADLINE>?
source: ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.

on_before_earliest.say: That date has already passed. Which day from today on would work for you?

on_invalid.say: Sorry, which exact date do you mean?

weekday_words.rule: 'Next <weekday>' means that weekday in the following calendar week. 'This <weekday>' means the one in the current week. So 'next Friday' said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
source: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week.
